title: The Consequences of Gen Z’s Risk Aversion | Institute for Family Studies
gist: Teaser of a Daily Signal piece (Katrina Trinko) on a new study linking risk tolerance to fertility: people more willing to take risks intend to have more children, and places with higher risk tolerance have higher fertility, raising the question of whether Gen Z's risk aversion implies fewer births.

insights.claim: A new study finds that people with more willingness to take risks intend to have more children.
insights.speaker: Katrina Trinko
insights.so_what: Risk preference may be a leading cultural indicator for fertility intentions.
insights.quote: people with more willingness to take risks also intend to have more kids.

insights.claim: The same study reports that at the geographic level, fertility is higher where people are more willing to take risks.
insights.speaker: Katrina Trinko
insights.so_what: Regional risk-attitude measures could help explain variation in birth rates.
insights.quote: where people are more willing to take risks, fertility is higher.

insights.claim: Gen Z's well-documented risk aversion, combined with the risk-fertility link, implies a possible further drag on American birth rates as this cohort enters prime childbearing years.
insights.speaker: Katrina Trinko
insights.so_what: Watch Gen Z fertility intentions; lower births feed long-run labor-force and consumer-demand projections.
